turns.text: Hey wizard, I'm getting an AE warning on the F3 work-roll bearing. Should I be worried?

JSR.HR.STD3.WR.BRG01.AE.RMS is at 8 dBuV - between the AE warning (6) and alarm (12), so stage-2 onset. AE is the leading indicator and crosses warning weeks before vibration. Not an emergency yet, but watch it closely.
What about the vibration and temperature?

Envelope BPFO is 3.2 g (above its 3.0 g alarm) and bearing temp is 102 degC (past the 100 degC trip). All three now agree: AE -> BPFO -> temp. That is the SCN-037 outer-race spall signature, now advanced.
Okay so what do I actually do?

Controlled stop (temp >100 degC), not an emergency trip. LOTO per SOP-01, hydraulic puller (never strike the bearing), inspect journal vs OEM H7/k6, induction-heat the new bearing 80-100 degC, laser-align <0.05 mm, replace labyrinth seal + coupling element, then verify <2.3 mm/s and <70 degC at 60 min.
F1 gearbox vibration alarm just came in. What's the reading?
JSR.HR.STD1.GBX01.VIB.GMF.RMS is at 11 mm/s, above the 10 mm/s alarm - a gross gear-mesh fault. Let me pull the oil data.
The chip detector also tripped.

Ferrous count is 60 ppm (alarm 40) and the chip trip means chunky spall debris. GMF + chip + 60 ppm Fe = tooth-root fatigue crack with active spalling, consistent with RCA-002 (usually after a high-torque cobble).
How urgent and what's the parts position?

Immediate controlled stop, no deferral - a fractured tooth can wreck the shaft. The problem is GEAR-WHL-M20 is 0 stock with a 36-week lead (critical path); BRG-GBX-SET is stock 1, 3-week. Unplanned cost ~USD 600k, ~168 h downtime. I'd recommend stocking the gear wheel as an insurance spare going forward.
F1 motor MCSA is reading -34 dBc. What does that mean?
JSR.HR.STD1.MTR01.MCSA.RBAR.SB at -34 dBc is past the -35 alarm (less-negative is worse) - a broken-rotor-bar fault per IEEE 1415. DE vibration with a 2x-slip component would confirm it.
Do I need to stop the motor right now?

No emergency stop. Broken-bar progression gives ~2-4 weeks; plan an insurance-spare swap (MTR-MV-6000, stock 1) within that window. Confirm via MCSA at steady load and verify phase rotation before energising the spare. Planned swap ~10 h, ~USD 100k.

required_facts: plan swap within 2-4 weeks not emergency stop

turns.text: Mould TC delta is 55 degC in a V-pattern. Is this a breakout?

TC delta 55 degC (alarm 50) in a V-pattern is the precursor, but a confirmed breakout needs the other two sensors too - a single sensor has >40% false-alarm rate. What are the oscillator friction and mould level?
Friction is 19 kN and level deviation is 13 mm.

Now all three agree (TC delta + friction 19 kN + level 13 mm) - this is a confirmed BPS breakout (SCN-043), P1. Reduce casting speed to minimum 0.5 m/min immediately; if it escalates, full emergency stop and evacuate the caster floor - liquid steel is fatal. Shell rupture can follow 60-90 s after the alarm.
BF blower discharge oscillation is at 9% and the anti-surge valve is cycling. What's happening?
PRES.OSC 9% is past the 8% alarm and the cycling ASV means the control is fighting an operating point left of the surge line - this is compressor surge (SCN-041), P1 on a 28 MW machine.
It's been surging for three cycles now. Should I keep trying to ride it out?

No - if surge persists beyond 2-3 cycles, trip immediately. Sustained surge is seconds-to-destruction. Do not restart until the cause (downstream valve slam / inlet filter fouling) is identified, then borescope IGVs/impellers and calibrate the anti-surge line. A surge failure runs ~USD 6M.

required_facts: trip if surge persists beyond 2-3 cycles
do not restart until cause identified

turns.text: Idler ultrasound on the ore conveyor is at 16 dBuV. Is that bad?
Yes - 16 dBuV is past the 15 alarm; ultrasound leads temperature, so this is a failing idler bearing. What is the idler surface temp?
Temp probe shows 100 degC on that idler.

That's the fire-risk alarm (100 degC). A seized idler under a loaded belt is the #1 belt-fire initiator (SCN-045). Stop the belt immediately, LOTO + belt-tension lock, lift the belt and replace the idler (IDLER-STD-1600, in stock), then confirm free rotation before restart.

required_facts: idler bearing seized / fire risk at 100 degC

turns.text: Ladle crane rope MFL is at 320 mV. Can I finish today's heats?

No. 320 mV is past the 300 mV ISO 4309:2017 discard alarm (>15-20% LMA). Take the crane out of service immediately - do not lift. Rope failure on a ladle crane means a molten-metal drop, a catastrophic P1 event.
There's a ladle hanging on it right now though.

Then lower that suspended load under control to a safe landing FIRST, then take the crane out of service - no further lifts. Call the crane Competent Person for inspection and certification, replace the rope (ROPE-CRN-01), and inspect drum/sheave grooves before any return to service.

required_facts: rope at ISO 4309 discard - do not lift
lower suspended load under control first

turns.text: Descale pump casing vibration is 5.4 mm/s and there's a spraying leak at the seal.
VIB.CAS.RMS 5.4 mm/s is past the 5.0 alarm and the spraying leak is the failure-stage symptom - this is mechanical seal failure (SCN-040), from abrasive scale-laden water wearing the faces.
What's the fix and do we have parts?

Switch to the standby pump, isolate + LOTO, back-pullout seal change. Parts: SEAL-MECH-DSC (stock 2, 2-week) and SLV-SHAFT-01 (stock 1, 3-week) - both on the shelf. Inspect the shaft sleeve, install the new SiC/SiC seal fingerprint-free, shaft runout <0.05 mm TIR. Event ~USD 14.4k.
Caster segment 7 roll rpm just hit 0 and clamping force is 540 kN. We're mid-cast.
Roll rpm 0 (no encoder pulses) with force 540 kN past the 480 warning is a roll seizure (SCN-042). The seized roll will drag the strand - transverse crack / breakout risk.
Can I pull the segment now to fix it?

Not while casting. First reduce casting speed if you're in the liquid-core zone, end the heat, and cool the strand 2-4 h before bay entry - then withdraw the segment via crane and replace the seized roll + bearings (BRG-SEG-01) and clear the spray nozzles. Set the segment gap per slab format and pressure-test.

required_facts: reduce speed / cool 2-4 h before entry
forbidden_claims: enter bay with liquid steel present

turns.text: AGC strip gauge is wandering - deviation up to 22 um. What's going on?
Gauge deviation 22 um is past the 20 alarm. Let me check the servo and oil. If position error is high and cleanliness is dirty, this is servo-valve silting.
Position error is 3.2% and ISO 4406 is 17/15/12.

That confirms it: ISO 17/15/12 (alarm) + position error 3.2% (alarm) + gauge 22 um = servo-valve silting / spool wear (SCN-048). Switch AGC to backup/manual lock, high-pressure LOTO, remove and ultrasonic-clean the valve (or replace SERVO-VLV-D661 if scored), replace the 3um filter and kidney-loop the oil to ISO 15/13/10, then step-response test.

required_facts: switch AGC to backup/manual + high-pressure LOTO

turns.text: Furnace flame signal dropped to 38% and fuel cut off. Can I just relight it?
Not directly. Flame signal below 40% triggered the auto fuel cutoff (SCN-046). Before any relight you must purge the furnace to clear unburnt fuel - relighting without a purge risks an explosion.
Okay purge is done. Then what?

Now clean or replace the burner nozzle (BURN-NOZ-01) and flame scanner (FLAME-SCAN-01), re-tune the fuel-air ratio, then relight per the burner-management sequence. Flue O2 should come back to 1.5-3.5%.

forbidden_claims: this is a refractory hot spot

turns.text: R1 force ripple is 8.5% and we're seeing periodic marks on the strip.
Force ripple 8.5% past the 8% alarm, periodic at 1x roll frequency with strip marks = work-roll spall/flat (SCN-044). Chock vibration would confirm the impact.
Chock vibration is 6 mm/s. What do we do with the strip already rolled?

Stop rolling spall-printed product and segregate that strip - the periodic marks make it defective. Quick-change the work rolls (15-45 min) using a prepared pair (WR-HSS-PREP, in stock), then send the removed roll to the roll shop to grind 3-5 mm below the spall, UT-test, and condemn if below minimum diameter.

required_facts: grind 3-5 mm below spall, UT test

turns.text: EAF HPU filter DP is at 4.5 bar. How bad is that?
That's the alarm/bypass threshold. The filter element is blinding - at the bypass, unfiltered oil reaches the servos (SCN-049). It's a P4 maintenance issue but act before the bypass opens.
What's the fix and how do we stop it recurring?

Isolate the HPU, replace the FLT-HYD-10 element set (in stock), clean the suction strainer and fit a desiccant breather to cut the EAF dust ingress, verify DP <1.5 bar on restart, and tighten the PM cadence to weekly.
Sinter fan 1x vibration just jumped from 1.8 to 7.1 mm/s. Bearing failing?

A sudden step jump to 7.1 mm/s (alarm) with axial 2x ratio rising to 0.4 is mass imbalance from deposit shedding (SCN-051), not a bearing spall - a spall would build gradually, not step. Asymmetric dust-cake shed off the rotor.
So how do we fix it?

Emergency stop, access the housing, manually clean the rotor deposits, then dynamic-balance online and trim with BAL-WT-01 (in stock). If it recurs, apply erosion-resistant hard-facing. Verify <4.5 mm/s after balancing.
BF cooling-water pump bearing temp is 100 degC and 1x vibration 5.6 mm/s.
Both at alarm (temp 100, 1x 5.6 mm/s) = pump bearing cage distress / fracture (SCN-050), often with a secondary seal weep and accelerated by suction water hammer.
We can't lose BF cooling. What's the move?

Switch to the standby cooling-water pump first, then isolate + LOTO the failing one. Disassemble, replace the bearing set + SEAL-MECH-DSC (stock 2), inspect the shaft for fretting, fit a suction-line surge damper, reassemble and align. That keeps BF cooling continuous.
The motor bearing is getting hot - I think it's the NDE bearing.
Okay, for the NDE bearing (SKF 6226) I'd trend the NDE vibration and temperature and prepare the BRG-MTR-SET DE+NDE bearing set. Can you give me the current readings?
No wait, it's the DE bearing, not the NDE - I misread the panel.

Got it - correcting to the DE bearing (SKF 6326). The plan still uses the BRG-MTR-SET (it covers both DE and NDE), but I'll focus the vibration/temperature trend on the DE end and the BPFO envelope at the DE bearing. Please share the DE readings.

required_facts: accepts the correction to DE bearing (SKF 6326)
refocuses the trend on the DE end
forbidden_claims: keeps analysing the NDE bearing after correction
claims DE and NDE are unrelated to this set

turns.text: F3 bearing temp is 102 - emergency-trip it, right?

Actually no - at >100 degC the correct action is a controlled stop, not an emergency trip. A sudden stop can thermally shock and crack the outer race. LOTO per SOP-01 and bring it down in a controlled way.
But the AE is also at 12 dBuV now, surely that changes it to an emergency trip?

AE 12 dBuV (at the alarm) raises urgency, but it does not change the stop method - it's still a controlled stop, faster but controlled, to avoid cracking the outer race. The AE alarm means act within hours, not that you slam-trip the drive.

required_facts: controlled stop not emergency trip even with AE alarm
forbidden_claims: switch to emergency trip because AE alarmed

turns.text: Mould oscillator friction is 19 kN - that's a confirmed breakout, evacuate now?

Friction 19 kN alone (past 18 alarm) is concerning but NOT a confirmed breakout - a single sensor has >40% false-alarm rate. A confirmed breakout needs TC delta V-pattern + friction + level all agreeing. What's the TC delta and mould level?
TC delta is only 18 degC and level is steady at 1 mm. So just friction is high.

Then this is NOT a breakout - with TC delta normal (18, below 25) and level steady, an isolated friction rise points to a mould-lubrication / taper issue (MAN-007 T4), not sticking. Investigate lubrication and oscillation; do not call a needless evacuation.

required_facts: single high friction is not a confirmed breakout

turns.text: Conveyor motor current is up to 106% and the belt's drifting. It's overloaded - clear the chute.

Let me check - at 106% FLA you're just over the 105 warning, not the 125% blocked-chute alarm, and you mentioned the belt is drifting (edge off-centre). That pattern is belt misalignment, where drift raises drive load - not a true chute overload.
Oh - so I shouldn't go looking at the chute?

Correct, the chute isn't the issue here. Fix the tracking instead: check the training/self-aligning idler and look for a seized return idler causing the lateral drift (RCA-023). A genuine chute block would push current toward 125%, which you're not seeing.

forbidden_claims: agrees it is a chute overload
sends them to clear the chute

turns.text: Gearbox GMF is at 5.5 mm/s. That's past alarm, schedule the gear-wheel change.
Let me check the threshold - GMF warning is 6.0 and alarm is 10.0 mm/s. 5.5 mm/s is actually below the warning, so it is not past alarm. A gear-wheel change would be unjustified here.
Ah, I was thinking of the 4.5 number. So we're fine?

The 4.5/7.1 numbers are the ISO 20816 bearing-velocity zones for other assets, not this gearbox's GMF band. At 5.5 mm/s GMF with normal oil Fe and no chip trip, the gearbox is healthy - continue routine GMF/cepstrum trending and monthly oil sampling. Reserve the 36-week-lead GEAR-WHL-M20 for a genuine alarm.

required_facts: 5.5 mm/s is below the 6.0 GMF warning

turns.text: Descale pump is noisy and vibration is up - it's cavitating.
Possibly, but let me confirm the signature. Cavitation shows low suction pressure (<70 kPa alarm) and high-frequency AE. What are the suction pressure and AE reading, and is there a leak at the seal?
Suction pressure is normal at 180 kPa, but there's a weep at the seal and bearing temp is climbing.

Then it's not cavitation - normal suction pressure rules that out. A weeping seal with rising casing vibration and bearing temp is mechanical seal failure (SCN-040). Switch to standby and plan the seal change (SEAL-MECH-DSC), not a cavitation/NPSH fix.

required_facts: normal suction pressure rules out cavitation
weep + vibration + temp = mechanical seal failure

turns.text: BF blower 1x vibration stepped up to 5.9 mm/s after a process upset - that's surge starting, trip it.

A 1x step to 5.9 mm/s after a transient is more likely a mass-imbalance from deposit shedding (RCA-017), not surge. Surge is defined by discharge-pressure oscillation >8% with axial bursts. What is the PRES.OSC reading?
Pressure oscillation is only 2%, totally stable.

Then it is not surge - with PRES.OSC at 2% (normal), this is a 1x mechanical imbalance from shed deposits. No immediate trip required; plan a rotor clean + field balance to bring 1x below 2.3 mm/s. Tripping the BF for a balance issue would be unnecessary.

forbidden_claims: trip the BF for the imbalance
confirms surge with normal pressure oscillation

turns.text: Crane rope MFL is 150 mV - that's the discard alarm, pull it out of service.

Let me check - 150 mV is the WARNING (~8-12% LMA, advisory), not the 300 mV discard alarm. At warning you increase inspection and plan, you don't have to remove it from service yet, unless a visual inspection shows discard-level broken wires.
Got it. And the visual shows 6 broken wires in one lay length - still fine?

That's still at the warning/advisory level per ISO 4309 - discard is >=12 random broken wires in one lay (or >=4 in one strand). 6 in one lay is advisory: tighten inspection frequency and plan a rope change, but it's not yet a mandatory discard. If it reaches 12-in-a-lay or MFL 300 mV, then it's discard / out of service.

required_facts: 150 mV is warning not discard alarm
discard is >=12 broken wires in one lay (or >=4 in one strand) / 300 mV
forbidden_claims: 6 broken wires in one lay = mandatory discard

turns.text: Flue O2 is high at 5.5% - the mixture is too rich, add more gas.

Actually high O2 means the opposite - too much air (lean / excess air), not rich. Adding more gas might help the ratio, but the real fix is to re-tune the fuel-air ratio / damper to bring O2 back to 1.5-3.5%. Is the flame stable and temperature on target?
Flame's stable, temperature is fine.

Then this is combustion imbalance / excess air (RCA family), not a burner failure. Re-tune the fuel-air ratio and check the air-damper / O2-trim loop. A LOW O2 (<1.0%) would be the rich condition - this is the high-O2 lean case.

required_facts: high O2 = excess air (lean), not rich
low O2 <1.0% would be the rich case
forbidden_claims: agrees to just add gas as the fix

turns.text: Segment clamping force is 500 kN - the roll has seized, pull the segment.
High force (500, past 480 warning) is concerning, but seizure specifically requires roll rpm dropping to 0. What is the ROLL.RPM right now?
Roll is still turning at about 4 rpm.

Then it has NOT seized - the roll is still rotating in its normal 3-25 rpm band. High force with normal rpm is segment misalignment / strand bulging (MAN-006 T3), not seizure. Re-set the segment gap and check alignment; watch the rpm - only if it drops to 0 does this become the seizure response.

forbidden_claims: confirms seizure with the roll still turning

turns.text: Gearbox oil viscosity is 268 cSt and temp is up - the gear teeth are cracking.

Let me separate those. High viscosity (268, past 265 alarm) with rising temp is an oil-condition issue - oxidation/varnish - not necessarily a tooth crack. A tooth crack shows high GMF vibration, Fe ppm and a chip trip. What are the GMF and Fe readings?
GMF is normal at 2.8 and Fe is 4 ppm, no chip trip.

Then it is NOT a tooth crack - normal GMF/Fe with no chip rules that out. This is oil oxidation / varnish (RCA-014). Do an oil service (drain/flush, fresh VG220, change filter), not a gear-wheel change. The 268 cSt is the oil degrading, not the gears.

required_facts: high viscosity = oil oxidation not tooth crack
normal GMF/Fe rules out tooth crack

turns.text: Motor PI test came back 4.0 - that's below the 1.5 alarm, insulation's failing.

Let me check the direction - for PI, HIGHER is better (2.0-5.0 is the healthy band; alarm is at 1.5, where LOWER is worse). A PI of 4.0 is actually healthy, well within normal. There's no insulation alarm here.
Oh I had it backwards. So 4.0 is good?

Yes - 4.0 indicates good, dry insulation. You'd only worry as PI falls toward 2.0 (warning) and 1.5 (alarm), which signals moisture/contamination. Keep the annual PI trend going; nothing to action at 4.0.

required_facts: higher PI is better; 4.0 is healthy

turns.text: AGC gauge deviation is 11 um and oil's at ISO 16/14/11 - it's full silting, pull the valve now.
Those are warning-stage numbers (gauge 11 just past 10 warning, ISO 16/14/11 is the warning level), not the 17/15/12 alarm with 3% position error of full silting. What's the position error?
Position error is still 0.9%.

Then pulling the valve now is premature - at POSERR 0.9% (below the 1.5 warning) the valve is still controlling. The right warning-stage action is oil remediation: replace the 3um filter and kidney-loop to ISO 15/13/10, then trend. Escalate to a valve clean/replace only if it reaches ISO 17/15/12 with POSERR >3%.

required_facts: POSERR below warning - valve still controlling
forbidden_claims: confirms full silting at warning numbers

turns.text: EAF HPU ISO 4406 is climbing - must be water ingress, fit a dehydrator.
Rising ISO 4406 on its own is particulate, not necessarily water - let me check the water reading. What is WATER.PPM, and is the oil hazy?
Water is normal at 80 ppm, oil's clear, but filter DP is also creeping up.

Then it's particulate ingress, not water - normal WATER.PPM and clear oil rule out water contamination. The right action is to kidney-loop filter the oil and fit a desiccant/particle breather to stop EAF dust ingress, plus pre-empt the filter (FLT-HYD-10) before DP reaches the 4.5 bar bypass. A dehydrator isn't needed for particulate.

required_facts: normal water rules out water contamination
forbidden_claims: confirms water ingress with normal WATER.PPM
fit a dehydrator as the fix

turns.text: R1 chock vibration and crown deviation are up - it's a work-roll spall, change the rolls.
Let me confirm against force ripple - a spall drives force ripple >8% at 1x roll with periodic strip marks. What is the force ripple, and are there periodic marks on the strip?
Force ripple is only 1.5% and no periodic marks - just the vibration and crown.

Then it's not a spall - low force ripple and no marks rule that out. Chock vibration + crown deviation with low force ripple is 5th-octave roll chatter (RCA-022), driven by below-optimal slab temperature into the stand resonance. Adjust the process (slab temp / speed), don't change the rolls.

required_facts: low force ripple rules out spall
forbidden_claims: confirms spall with low force ripple

turns.text: BF cooling pump head is down 8% - the bearing's failing, switch pumps.
Head deviation -8% points to a hydraulic issue, but let me check the bearing before concluding. What's the bearing temperature and 1x vibration?
Bearing temp's normal at 60 and 1x vibration is fine.

Then the bearing isn't failing - normal temp and 1x rule that out. Negative head deviation with a healthy bearing is impeller wear / erosion (RCA-019). You can plan an impeller (IMP-CW-01) + wear-ring change at a window rather than an urgent pump swap - it's a performance loss, not a bearing emergency.

required_facts: normal bearing temp/1x rules out bearing failure
impeller wear from negative head deviation
plan impeller change, not urgent swap
forbidden_claims: confirms bearing failure with normal bearing readings
this is the SCN-050 bearing mode

turns.text: Rip-loop is reading 70 mA - that's the rip alarm, stop the belt.
Let me check - the rip alarm is at 0 mA (open loop = severed conductor). 70 mA is actually within the normal 60-80 mA band, so there's no rip alarm. Is there something else prompting the concern?
Oh I misread it - it's actually showing 0 mA.

Then yes - 0 mA IS the rip alarm: the embedded conductor is severed, indicating a longitudinal tear. Stop the belt immediately, LOTO + belt-tension lock, inspect the full length and repair (cold-bond or vulcanised splice) before restart.

required_facts: 70 mA is normal, 0 mA is the rip alarm
after correction to 0 mA, stop belt immediately

turns.text: F3 bearing OFB outlet temp is 87 and bearing temp 103 - it's an outer-race spall, BPFO must be high.
Before assuming a spall, let me check the BPFO envelope - a spall drives BPFO energy up first. What's the envelope BPFO reading?
BPFO is actually normal, around 0.3 g.

Then it's not a spall - normal BPFO rules that out. High OFB outlet temp (87, past 85 alarm) + bearing temp with low BPFO is lubrication starvation / oil-film breakdown (RCA-013). Controlled stop on the temperature, then clear the lube nozzle (LUBE-NOZ-01) and check oil-film supply - don't go straight to a bearing replacement.

required_facts: lube starvation from high OFB temp + low BPFO
forbidden_claims: confirms outer-race spall with normal BPFO

turns.text: Winding temp is 156 - the rotor bar must be broken, swap the motor.

A high winding temp (156, past 155 alarm) is a thermal symptom, not a broken-bar one - a broken bar shows in the MCSA sideband, not the winding temperature. What's the MCSA reading, and was there a long heavy campaign?
MCSA is normal, and yes we just ran a 14-hour heavy campaign.

Then it's not a broken rotor bar - normal MCSA rules that out. This is winding overheat from the extended campaign exceeding thermal capacity (RCA-015). De-rate / pause to cool below 130 degC, check the cooling path, and update the VFD thermal model for the aged winding. No motor swap needed.

required_facts: normal MCSA rules out broken rotor bar
forbidden_claims: confirms broken rotor bar from winding temp

turns.text: Segment spray flow dropped to 144 - just a sensor glitch, ignore it.

I'd be cautious about dismissing it - 144 L/min is below the 150 warning. A real spray-flow drop is usually nozzle scale blockage, and it's the upstream cause that can lead to roll seizure if cooling is lost. Is there any bulge developing or roll-rotation change?
Now that you mention it, there's a small bulge appearing.

Then it's not a glitch - a real cooling deficit. Spray-nozzle blockage (RCA-021) with a developing bulge is the precursor to roll seizure (RCA-006). Clear/replace the nozzles (NOZ-SPRAY-01) now to restore 180-220 L/min and address the hard-water scale source, before it thermally overloads the roll bearing.

required_facts: does not dismiss the spray-flow drop
forbidden_claims: agrees it is a sensor glitch to ignore

turns.text: F3 bearing pe AE warning aa raha hai, tension ki baat hai kya?
AE.RMS 8 dBuV pe hai - warning (6) aur alarm (12) ke beech, stage-2 onset. AE leading indicator hai, vibration se weeks pehle warning deta hai. Abhi emergency nahi, par closely watch karo.
Vibration aur temperature ka kya scene hai?
Envelope BPFO 3.2 g (alarm 3.0 ke upar) aur bearing temp 102 degC (trip 100 ke upar). Ab teeno agree kar rahe: AE -> BPFO -> temp. Ye SCN-037 outer-race spall signature hai, advanced stage.
Toh ab kya karu?

Controlled stop (temp >100), emergency trip nahi - achanak stop se thermal shock outer race crack kar sakta hai. SOP-01 ke hisab se LOTO, hydraulic puller, journal H7/k6 check, naya bearing induction-heat 80-100, laser align <0.05mm, labyrinth seal + coupling replace, phir 60 min pe <2.3 mm/s aur <70 degC verify.
F1 gearbox vibration alarm aaya hai. Reading kya hai?
JSR.HR.STD1.GBX01.VIB.GMF.RMS 11 mm/s pe hai, alarm 10 ke upar - gross gear-mesh fault. Oil data bhi pull karta hu.
Chip detector bhi trip ho gaya.

Fe count 60 ppm (alarm 40) + chip trip = chunky spall debris. GMF + chip + 60 ppm Fe = tooth-root fatigue crack with active spalling (RCA-002), aksar high-torque cobble ke baad. Turant controlled stop, koi deferral nahi - tooth fracture shaft damage kar sakta hai.
Parts ka kya scene hai?

Problem yahi hai: GEAR-WHL-M20 stock 0, 36-week lead (critical path); BRG-GBX-SET stock 1, 3-week. Unplanned ~USD 600k, ~168 h downtime. Aage ke liye gear wheel ko insurance spare ke roop mein stock karne ki recommend karta hu.
Motor bearing garam ho raha, mujhe lagta hai NDE bearing hai.
Theek hai, NDE bearing (SKF 6226) ke liye NDE vibration aur temp trend karunga aur BRG-MTR-SET ready rakhunga. Current readings batao.
Ruko, NDE nahi DE bearing hai - maine panel galat padh liya.

Samajh gaya - DE bearing (SKF 6326) pe correct kar raha hu. Plan wahi BRG-MTR-SET use karega (DE aur NDE dono cover karta hai), par ab vibration/temp trend DE end pe aur BPFO envelope DE bearing pe focus karunga. DE readings bhejiye.
Mould friction 19 kN hai - confirmed breakout hai na, evacuate kar du?

Sirf friction 19 kN (alarm 18) chinta ki baat hai par confirmed breakout NAHI - single sensor >40% false alarm deta hai. Confirmed breakout ke liye TC delta V-pattern + friction + level teeno chahiye. TC delta aur mould level kya hai?
TC delta sirf 18 degC hai aur level steady 1 mm pe.

Toh ye breakout NAHI - TC delta normal (18, 25 se neeche) aur level steady ke saath, isolated friction rise mould-lubrication/taper issue hai (MAN-007 T4), sticking nahi. Lubrication aur oscillation check karo; bekaar evacuation mat karo.

required_facts: single high friction is not confirmed breakout

turns.text: BF blower discharge oscillation 9% pe hai aur ASV cycle kar raha. Kya ho raha hai?
PRES.OSC 9% alarm (8) ke upar hai aur cycling ASV matlab control surge line ke left wale operating point se lad raha - ye compressor surge (SCN-041), 28 MW machine pe P1.
Teen cycle ho gaye surge ke. Ride out kar lu kya?

Nahi - agar surge 2-3 cycle se zyada chale to turant trip karo. Sustained surge seconds-to-destruction hai. Cause (downstream valve slam / inlet filter fouling) identify hone tak restart mat karo, phir IGV/impeller borescope aur anti-surge line calibrate. Surge failure ~USD 6M.

required_facts: trip if surge persists beyond 2-3 cycles
cause identify hone tak restart nahi

turns.text: Ladle crane rope MFL 150 mV pe hai - ye discard alarm hai, crane out karo.

Ruko - 150 mV WARNING hai (~8-12% LMA, advisory), 300 mV discard alarm nahi. Warning pe inspection badhao aur plan karo, abhi service se hatana zaroori nahi - jab tak visual inspection mein discard-level broken wires na dikhe.
Visual mein ek lay mein 6 broken wires dikh rahe - phir bhi theek?

Wo abhi bhi warning/advisory level hai ISO 4309 ke hisab se - discard >=12 random broken wires ek lay mein (ya >=4 ek strand mein). 6 ek lay mein advisory hai: inspection frequency tight karo aur rope change plan karo, par mandatory discard nahi. 12-in-a-lay ya MFL 300 mV pe ye discard / out-of-service ban jaata.

required_facts: discard >=12 broken wires in one lay (or >=4 in strand) / 300 mV

turns.text: Conveyor idler ultrasound 16 dBuV pe hai. Bura hai kya?
Haan - 16 dBuV alarm (15) ke upar; ultrasound temperature se lead karta hai, toh failing idler bearing hai. Idler surface temp kya hai?
Us idler pe temp 100 degC dikh raha.

Wo fire-risk alarm hai (100 degC). Loaded belt ke neeche seized idler #1 belt-fire initiator hai (SCN-045). Belt turant band karo, LOTO + belt-tension lock, belt lift karke idler replace karo (IDLER-STD-1600, stock mein), phir restart se pehle free rotation confirm.

required_facts: idler seized / fire risk at 100 degC

turns.text: Motor PI test 4.0 aaya - ye 1.5 alarm se neeche hai, insulation fail ho rahi.
Direction check karte hain - PI mein HIGHER better hai (2.0-5.0 healthy; alarm 1.5 pe hai jaha LOWER worse hai). 4.0 toh actually healthy hai, normal band mein. Yahan koi insulation alarm nahi.
Oh maine ulta samajh liya. Toh 4.0 acha hai?

Haan - 4.0 acha, dry insulation dikhata hai. Chinta tab jab PI 2.0 (warning) aur 1.5 (alarm) ki taraf gire, jo moisture/contamination ka sign hai. Annual PI trend chalu rakho; 4.0 pe kuch action nahi.
Gearbox GMF 5.5 mm/s pe hai. Ye alarm ke upar hai, gear-wheel change schedule karo.
Threshold check karte hain - GMF warning 6.0 aur alarm 10.0 mm/s hai. 5.5 toh warning ke bhi neeche hai, alarm ke upar nahi. Gear-wheel change yahan unjustified hoga.
Achha, mai 4.5 number soch raha tha. Toh hum theek hain?

4.5/7.1 toh ISO 20816 bearing-velocity zones hain doosre assets ke liye, is gearbox ke GMF band ke nahi. 5.5 mm/s GMF, normal Fe aur koi chip trip nahi - gearbox healthy hai. Routine GMF/cepstrum trending aur monthly oil sampling chalu rakho. 36-week-lead GEAR-WHL-M20 ko genuine alarm ke liye reserve rakho.
Furnace flame signal 38% pe gir gaya aur fuel cut ho gaya. Seedha relight kar du?
Seedha nahi. Flame signal 40% se neeche auto fuel cutoff hua (SCN-046). Relight se pehle furnace purge karna zaroori hai unburnt fuel clear karne ke liye - bina purge relight explosion risk hai.
Theek hai purge ho gaya. Ab?
Ab burner nozzle (BURN-NOZ-01) aur flame scanner (FLAME-SCAN-01) clean/replace karo, fuel-air ratio re-tune karo, phir burner-management sequence se relight. Flue O2 1.5-3.5% pe wapas aana chahiye.
Descale pump noisy hai aur vibration up - cavitation ho raha hoga.
Ho sakta hai, par signature confirm karte hain. Cavitation mein suction pressure low (<70 kPa alarm) aur high-frequency AE hota hai. Suction pressure aur AE kya hai, aur seal pe leak hai kya?
Suction pressure normal 180 kPa, par seal pe weep hai aur bearing temp chadh raha.

Toh ye cavitation NAHI - normal suction pressure usse rule out karta hai. Weeping seal + rising casing vibration + bearing temp = mechanical seal failure (SCN-040). Standby pe switch karo aur seal change plan karo (SEAL-MECH-DSC), cavitation/NPSH fix nahi.

required_facts: weep + vibration + temp = mechanical seal failure
forbidden_claims: normal suction ke baad bhi cavitation confirm

turns.text: Segment 7 roll rpm 0 ho gaya aur force 540 kN. Hum mid-cast hain.
Roll rpm 0 (no encoder pulses) + force 540 kN (480 warning ke upar) = roll seizure (SCN-042). Seized roll strand ko drag karega - transverse crack / breakout risk.
Abhi segment pull kar lu fix karne?

Casting ke dauraan nahi. Pehle liquid-core zone mein ho to casting speed kam karo, heat end karo, strand 2-4 h cool karo bay entry se pehle - phir crane se segment withdraw karke seized roll + bearings (BRG-SEG-01) replace aur spray nozzles clear karo. Segment gap slab format ke hisab se set aur pressure-test.

required_facts: speed kam + 2-4 h cool before entry
forbidden_claims: liquid steel ke saath bay enter

turns.text: EAF HPU ISO 4406 chadh raha - water ingress hoga, dehydrator lagao.
Sirf ISO 4406 chadhna particulate ho sakta hai, zaroori nahi water - water reading check karte hain. WATER.PPM kya hai, aur oil hazy hai kya?
Water normal 80 ppm, oil clear, par filter DP bhi creep kar raha.

Toh ye particulate ingress hai, water nahi - normal WATER.PPM aur clear oil water contamination ko rule out karte hain. Sahi action: kidney-loop filter karo aur desiccant/particle breather lagao EAF dust ingress rokne ke liye, aur filter (FLT-HYD-10) DP 4.5 bar bypass se pehle change karo. Particulate ke liye dehydrator nahi chahiye.

required_facts: normal water rules out water contamination
forbidden_claims: normal water ke baad bhi water ingress confirm

turns.text: Pump kharab lag raha, kya karu?
Do pump hain - HSM.DSC.PMP01 (HP descaling) aur BF.CW.PMP02 (BF cooling-water). Pehle batao kaunsa pump, aur kya symptom/reading hai (vibration, bearing temp, suction pressure)?
BF cooling-water wala, bearing temp 86 degC pe hai aur vibration thoda up.

Theek hai - BF.CW.PMP02. Temp 86 (warning 85 ke upar) + rising broadband vibration early bearing distress hai, abhi 100 degC / 5.6 mm/s alarm nahi - warning stage. Standby pump available rakho, bearing + seal change plan karo (SEAL-MECH-DSC, stock 2). Agar 100 degC / 1x 5.6 mm/s -> turant standby pe switch + isolate.
R1 chock vibration aur crown deviation up hai - work-roll spall hai, rolls change karo.
Force ripple ke against confirm karte hain - spall force ripple >8% 1x roll pe driv karta hai with periodic strip marks. Force ripple kya hai, aur strip pe periodic marks hain?
Force ripple sirf 1.5% hai aur koi periodic marks nahi - bas vibration aur crown.

Toh spall NAHI - low force ripple aur no marks usse rule out karte hain. Chock vibration + crown deviation with low force ripple = 5th-octave roll chatter (RCA-022), below-optimal slab temperature ki wajah se stand resonance mein. Process adjust karo (slab temp / speed), rolls change mat karo.

required_facts: low force ripple rules out spall
forbidden_claims: low force ripple ke baad bhi spall confirm

turns.text: What's the F3 bearing vibration alarm again?
JSR.HR.STD3.WR.BRG01.VIB.DE.H.RMS alarm is 7.1 mm/s (warning 4.5), ISO 20816-3 Group 2. Anything you want me to check against it?
And remind me which spare we'd need if it spalls?
For the SCN-037 outer-race spall you'd need BRG-LRG-300 (stock 1, 8-week), plus SEAL-LAB-01 and CPL-EL-01 - all in stock. Same bearing job we discussed for this asset.
Good. Is the bearing change a controlled stop or a trip?
Controlled stop - consistent with what applies to this F3 bearing: above 100 degC you stop in a controlled way (not an emergency trip) to avoid thermal-shock cracking of the outer race, per SOP-01.
I've got two warnings at once - the F3 bearing AE and the F1 gearbox GMF. Which first?

Both are early warnings, but the gearbox path is the bigger exposure: a tooth crack (SCN-038) runs ~USD 600k / 168 h and its gear wheel (GEAR-WHL-M20) is stock 0 with a 36-week lead. The F3 bearing (SCN-037) is ~USD 90k with BRG-LRG-300 in stock. Action the gearbox first.
What do I actually do on the gearbox to confirm?

Confirm the gearbox via oil Fe ppm and the chip detector alongside the GMF - if Fe climbs toward 40 ppm or the chip detector trips, it's the tooth-crack path and you stage for a controlled stop. Keep the F3 AE on daily trend in parallel.

required_facts: confirm gearbox via Fe ppm + chip detector

turns.text: Show me the EAF HPU vibration trend.

The EAF auxiliary HPU (EAF.AUX.HYD01) doesn't have a vibration sensor - its channels are ISO 4406 cleanliness, oil temp, filter DP and water ppm. There's no vibration trend for it. Did you mean the filter DP or the cleanliness trend?
Right, sorry - show me the filter DP trend then.

Sure - I'll pull the FILT.DP trend (normal 0-1.5 bar, warning 3.0, alarm/bypass 4.5). If it's trending toward 4.5 the element is blinding (SCN-049) and you'd want to change FLT-HYD-10 before the bypass opens.

forbidden_claims: a vibration threshold for this asset

turns.text: Spray flow on segment 7 has been falling for days, now 150. Where's this heading?

Falling spray flow is nozzle scale blockage (RCA-021), and it reduces secondary cooling. If uncorrected, the roll/bearing temperature climbs and can thermally overload the roll bearing toward seizure (RCA-006 / SCN-042). Is roll rotation still steady?
Rolls are still turning normally for now.

Good - so you're upstream of seizure. Clear/replace the nozzles (NOZ-SPRAY-01) now to restore 180-220 L/min and fix the hard-water scale source. Keep watching roll rpm + clamping force; if rpm heads to 0 / force >480 kN, it becomes the SCN-042 seizure response.

required_facts: spray blockage -> cooling loss -> seizure path

turns.text: Is the F1 motor safe to keep running?
I can't say safe or unsafe without readings - it depends on WIND.TEMP, MCSA sideband, vibration, current imbalance and PI. Can you share the live values or a recent trend?
Winding temp 120, MCSA -58, vibration 1.8, current imbalance 0.6%.

Those are all in the healthy band: winding 120 (normal 80-130), MCSA -58 (normal, far from the -35 alarm), vibration 1.8 (normal), current imbalance 0.6% (normal). Yes - the motor is safe to run on these readings; continue routine monitoring.

required_facts: all four readings in healthy band
forbidden_claims: flags an alarm on healthy values

turns.text: Mould heat flux is slowly dropping over the campaign toward 1.0, TC delta and friction normal. Breakout risk?

Not an acute breakout - that needs the TC V-pattern + friction + level agreeing. A slow heat-flux decline with normal TC/friction is gradual copper-plate wear (poorer shell-to-mould transfer), a planned-maintenance item.
So when do I change the plates?

Plan a mould copper-plate change (MOLD-CU-STD) at the next campaign boundary - note it's a 14-week-lead item (stock 1), so order ahead. Keep trending heat flux vs the 1.0/0.8 thresholds and confirm it recovers to 1.2-2.0 MW/m2 after the change.

required_facts: copper plate wear not acute breakout

turns.text: Crane gearbox GMF vibration is 1.1 g. Same as the rope problem we had?

No - that's a different mode. 1.1 g (past the 1.0 warning) on GBX.VIB.GMF is hoist-gearbox gear wear, separate from the wire-rope MFL and the brake-temp modes. The rope issue is its own discard-criteria call.
Okay so what for the gearbox?

Pull an FFT for GMF sidebands and a gearbox oil sample, plan a gearbox inspection/service, and trend GBX.VIB.GMF against the 2.5 g alarm. Important but not the immediate P1 rope/brake hazard - keep those checks current too.

required_facts: gearbox gear wear is a different mode from the rope
FFT + oil sample, inspect before 2.5 g alarm
forbidden_claims: conflates it with the wire-rope discard

turns.text: After the last surge the ASV opened and vibration settled. Can I ramp back to full load now?

Not blindly. The ASV catching one surge doesn't mean the root cause is fixed - SCN-041 explicitly says don't restart/ramp until the cause (valve slam / inlet filter fouling) is identified. Ramping back could re-enter surge.
Understood - what's the safe sequence to get back to load?

Hold at a reduced/safe load, identify and correct the surge cause, borescope the IGVs/impellers and run ferrography on the oil, calibrate the anti-surge line vs OEM data, then ramp under rotating-equipment-engineer authorisation. Don't go straight to full load.

required_facts: do not ramp until cause identified

turns.text: Which of our failure scenarios are the P1 safety-critical ones I should brief the shift on?

The four P1 failure scenarios are: BF blower compressor surge (SCN-041), caster mould breakout (SCN-043), ore-conveyor idler belt-fire (SCN-045), and ladle-crane wire-rope failure (SCN-047). These are the safety-critical ones.
And which of those has a stocking gap I should flag?

Of those, the BF blower's anti-surge valve (ASV-VLV-01) is stock 0 with a 12-week lead - a real stocking gap behind a P1 / ~USD 6M failure. The mould (MOLD-CU-STD 14-week), conveyor idler (in stock) and crane rope (ROPE-CRN-01, stock 1) are better covered. Flag the ASV for a stocking review.
F3 bearing temp is rising ~5 degC/hr at steady load, now 78. Run to end of campaign?

A sustained >5 degC/hr rise is the SOP-01 'accelerated monitoring / plan change within 24 h' trigger, even though 78 is below the 85 warning. I wouldn't commit to end-of-campaign. What are BPFO and OFB outlet temp?
BPFO normal, OFB outlet 80.

Normal BPFO with an elevated OFB outlet points to a lube/thermal issue (RCA-013), not a spall. Check lube supply pressure and the lube nozzle (LUBE-NOZ-01) for blockage, accelerate monitoring, and plan a controlled change within 24 h. If temp reaches 100 degC, controlled stop immediately - don't run open-ended.

required_facts: >5 degC/hr triggers plan change within 24 h
controlled stop at 100 degC, not open-ended
